summary: file pattern lang and domain are interpolated into the event JSON unescaped; a quote in file writes a permanently malformed line to the append-only log
all-or-nothing is only true of validator rejection; record appends inside the loop and the loop has a reachable exit 2, so a poisoned batch writes rows then fails
nothing invokes --json and both skills still say to pipe a Findings (recordable) block that no reviewer emits now, so the loop this task exists to close is still open
a 0x1f in file is not stripped, shifts the columns, and puts a non-numeric into the bare line position, producing malformed JSON in the committed log
the comment claims normalise_summary makes the separator byte impossible in any value; it is applied only to summary, and file pattern lang domain reach the same stream raw
the comment says the summary normalisation is what makes this printf safe; the printf takes four other reviewer-controlled fields that nothing normalises
zero findings and rejected batches emit only stderr, never a finding-gap event, so kit-status.sh line 396 reports a gap count pinned at zero once the harvester is deleted
the validator-reads-the-vocabulary check asserts only a non-zero exit, so it passes on a failed cp, a missing python3, or a syntax error, with no positive control
--contract sits inside the arg loop after kit_root and kit_active, so outside an active project it prints nothing and exits 0, unlike --vocab which is handled at line 28
the step named contract-defined-in-one-place never compares agents against --contract, while all four agents restate the field list the comment forbids restating
--batch and the single-flag path still call record with five args, so summary is empty; the bare-counter row this change exists to abolish is creatable at both documented doors
the wiring proof says the fix was disallowing a tool and stating the output rule as overriding; neither string is in agents, skills or hooks and the frontmatter is untouched
jf and jn take the first match, so 40 chars of reviewer-controlled lang can inject a model, line or summary key that the indexer prefers over the real one and still parses
summary, file_path and line_no have no reader; no report, query or accelerator selects them, so the stated benefit needs hand-written SQL to reach
the subshell chains only cd and git init with &&; with no set -e a failed cd would run kit-init, write T-j.md and commit inside the kit's own repository
subprocess.run has no timeout, so a hung --vocab hangs the recorder, and a missing bash raises an uncaught FileNotFoundError instead of Rejected
the --vocab printf format is duplicated at lines 28 and 53, two copies that must agree inside the file whose whole premise is one definition
skills/checkpoint/SKILL.md tells operators to pipe a `Findings (recordable)` block via --batch; reviewers now emit JSON only, so the documented recording path cannot work.
skills/verify-ladder/SKILL.md has the identical stale instruction: pipe a `Findings (recordable)` block via --batch, a format none of the four rewritten reviewer contracts produce.
record() escapes only `summary`; lang/pattern/file are interpolated unescaped into the event JSON, so a quote or backslash there corrupts the committed events.ndjson line.
The --json write loop appends one record() per finding via separate writes; a crash or a corrupted later field leaves earlier findings committed, breaking all-or-nothing.
tooling/kit-review-findings.sh, which the task record says 'is being deleted, not repaired,' still exists on disk with its five previously-filed defects intact.
The hostile-input test sends a hostile char only in `summary`; pattern/file/lang reach the same unescaped printf but are never tested, so the corruption above is invisible to CI.
agents/tester.md omits the explicit 'no prose, no code fence' framing the other three reviewer contracts carry (e.g. implementation-reviewer.md:54); unfence() covers it, but it's inconsistent.
a rejected batch still emits no finding-gap: main returns 2 with empty stdout, so the one case where findings are really lost stays a stderr line
the only gap event the new writer can emit means zero findings, but the report reads it as reviews that emitted findings none of which were recorded
the single append is unchecked: an unwritable or full events.ndjson still prints recorded N findings and exits 0, and a large batch flushes in several writes
outside an active project the recorder exits 0 before reading stdin, so a piped review is destroyed silently and the caller sees success
sanitise says it is applied to every string reaching the log; task is written raw on both event kinds, so a quoted task id aborts with an internal error
the --contract reachability fix has no test: the step runs it inside the kit repo, which has a profile, so moving it back into the arg loop stays green
deleting --batch was not swept through the backlog: an open task still carries an acceptance criterion requiring --batch to accept a new field
--vocab and --contract were dropped from the arg loop and now work only as the first argument; kit-finding.sh --task T --vocab exits 2 as unknown

12 of 13 `( cd '$X' && git init ...)` subshells in conformance.sh still lack the `|| exit 1` guard; only the one instance a T3 reviewer flagged (now :1182) was fixed, unswept everywhere else in the...
Docstring claims sanitise() covers every string field reaching the log, 'not only summary'; `task` is written raw in build_events/gap_event and bypasses it entirely.
`opts['task']` is inserted into the event dict unsanitised, unlike agent/agent_id/model on the same line; a hostile value fails only via the generic _assert_flat backstop, not a task-specific check.
Same unsanitised `task` field in the finding-gap event; identical asymmetry with agent/agent_id.
emit() claims one atomic append settles all-or-nothing, but the exit status of `printf ... >> '$EV'` is never checked; a full-disk or unwritable-$EV failure still reports success.
Broken-command exits are recorded under gap reason 'rejected', whose displayed text falsely claims a malformed field
If the recorder refuses a reply the validator accepted, a gap event may be written twice for one failure
Tail-of-script gap append lacks mkdir -p, silently dropping the gap on a non-default unwritten state dir
A missing or unreadable --prompt-file is ignored, so the loop reviews an EMPTY prompt; an empty reply records reason=empty and exits 0, reading as a clean review
pipefail makes a compliant review look like a broken command when the reviewer does not drain stdin: printf dies of SIGPIPE, the reply is discarded and a false gap recorded
A validator failure that is not Rejected (missing python3, undecodable reply) is read as a refusal and the loop resends an EMPTY prompt for every remaining attempt
The exit-3 versus exit-2 distinction the comment says protects the caller is never read: the only caller tests success or failure alone
ATTR is unquoted at three sites, so a task id with whitespace or a glob breaks the recorder AND the gap call, and the review is lost with no row at all
The tail gap append is unchecked and does not mkdir the state dir, so a full or missing path loses the gap silently -- the check kit-finding.sh added in round 4
The INT trap deletes WORKDIR without exiting, so Ctrl-C is recorded as a rejected finding-gap in the committed log instead of cancelling the run
The fixture asserts gap COUNT but never reason, task or agent, and builds none of the non-draining, missing-prompt-file or validator-failure paths the Verified section implies
A gap already written by the emit path in kit-finding.sh is written a second time at the tail, so one failed review can count as two gaps
No timeout and no output cap on the reviewer command: the bound counts attempts only, so one hung or runaway call is unbounded in time and disk
The mktemp fallback path under TMPDIR is predictable and mkdir -p accepts a pre-created or symlinked directory, so a local user can read or substitute the reviewer reply
Reviewer-controlled text is interpolated into the correction prompt sent back to a model, so a crafted field name can carry instructions into the retry (OWASP LLM01)
